podcast.title: Advocating "Midwestern Sound"
podcast.body: Mike Reilly, as of June 2021, continues to resist the "country rock" label for Pure Prairie League, preferring to define their music as the "midwestern sound." This label reflects their diverse musical background in Cincinnati, which included jazz, blues, country, bluegrass, R&B, and soul, and their wide-ranging influences from The Beatles to Lonnie Mack, as well as The Byrds and Poco. "Mike Riley also resist that country rock label even today in June of twenty twenty one he said that the band prefers to think of it as the midwestern sound."

podcast.title: Stepping Up in Pure Prairie League
podcast.body: Mike Reilly joined Pure Prairie League and "stepped up" to take leadership, "grabbing the reins" to steer the band after co-founder Craig Fuller's legal problems led to RCA dropping the group. He helped the band navigate a difficult period. "Mike Riley joined the band and he said I basically stepped up I think by default and grabbed the reins and kept trying to steer the buggy"
